clue.text: Curtailment of overdue preparation to eat

indicators.note: a preparation is something worked up or made ready, so the trimmed letters are worked into a new order
curtailing a word cuts off its tail, so the final letter of overdue goes

explanation.surface: Someone is cutting short an overdue bit of cookery so they can finally eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailment of' drops the last E of OVERDUE, leaving OVERDU; 'preparation' rearranges those six letters. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour is to eat greedily, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Veto on setter's entry into parliament left ass, maybe, but not Balaam's

indicators.note: the veto and the setter make their entry into the parliament, so they go inside its letters

parts.note: the Duma is the Russian parliament
to veto is to ban
the setter's = I'm, the setter speaking of himself

explanation.surface: A ban on the setter entering parliament has left him looking like an ass.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's reads as 'setter is', the setter's I'M. In the Bible Balaam's ass spoke, so it was the one ass that could not be called mute.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is an example of a creature without speech; the exception for Balaam's ass, which spoke, makes the definition precise.

clue.text: Wish on departure for movement of sea to swamp Scots river

indicators.note: the sea movement swamps the river by surrounding it, so its letters wrap the other piece

parts.note: a swell is the heaving movement of the sea
the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A farewell wish that the sea's surge may not flood a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'stay well' is a parting wish for someone's continued good health.

clue.text: Get weapon back first with gold piece

indicators.note: first says the turned weapon comes before the other piece, despite the clue's order
back tells us the weapon's word is read from right to left

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

explanation.surface: An instruction to retrieve your weapon before going after the gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GUN into NUG, and 'first' puts it ahead of GET, which is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a lump of native gold, so a piece of gold.

clue.text: Glen with fragments often shed by discovery

indicators.note: breaking words into fragments lets their letters be put back together in another order

explanation.surface: A Scottish valley strewn with fragments that a discovery has scattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fragments' rearranges the eight letters. The definition is a phrase the answer completes: a discovery sheds this on a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is commonly said to shed fresh understanding on a subject, the idiom being completed by the answer.

clue.text: Admit and confess on 8

parts.note: to admit a point is to grant it
to own up is to confess, so own means confess

explanation.surface: An instruction to admit and confess to something, attached to a numbered reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is SPEY, so 'on 8' means a place on the Spey: Grantown-on-Spey is a Highland town on that river.
explanation.definitionFit: Grantown-on-Spey is a Scottish town standing on the river of 8-down, so its name fits being on that river.

clue.text: Barbarian with hairpiece chasing girl

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders, so a Hun is a barbarian
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A barbarian with a lock of hair is pursuing a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing girl' looks like the barbarian's action, but read together it is the definition: a girl who hunts.
explanation.definitionFit: A huntress is a woman who hunts, so a female doing the chasing.

clue.text: Bird of wilderness and loughs

indicators.note: of is taken as 'from inside', so the bird is lifted out of the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A bird that lives in the wild and around the lakes of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and loughs' adds a second hint rather than letters: Lough Erne is a pair of lakes in Northern Ireland, a lough being an Irish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a large bird.

clue.text: River round which to dance when consent's arising

indicators.note: in a down clue arising means going up, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: yep is a casual yes, a word of consent, and the 's gives the S

explanation.surface: A river around which people dance whenever agreement is reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link. The strathspey, a Scottish dance, is named after the valley (strath) round this river.
explanation.definitionFit: The strathspey takes its name from the strath of this Scottish river, so the dance happens round it in name.

clue.text: So (in response) … first of words frequently found between covers

indicators.note: first of picks only the opening letter of the word that follows
the frequency word is found between the two coverings, so it sits in the middle

parts.note: a hat covers the head
the plural covers gives a second hat
oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: A dismissive reply about words that keep turning up between book covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' is plural, so it supplies two HATs, with OFT between them, after the W from 'first of words'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So what?' is a dismissive reply, and the answer phrase is a fuller way of saying the same thing.

clue.text: Heartless church article on church in suspension

indicators.note: losing its heart means the centre letter of the church word is dropped

parts.note: an abbey is a monastic church
an is the indefinite article
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church without heart is suspended along with an item about the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle B of ABBEY to give ABEY. 'on' and 'in' are links; 'in suspension' is the idiom 'in abeyance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyance is a state of temporary suspension, as in a matter held in abeyance.

clue.text: Junction in Crete dismantled without an oath

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters surround the oath
something dismantled is taken apart and could be reassembled differently

parts.note: 'hang it!' is a mild oath, so hang can stand for one

explanation.surface: A road junction in Crete being taken apart without anyone swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismantled' makes TERCE from the island's letters, and 'without' (outside) puts that round the oath; IN stays as written at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An interchange is a road junction where routes cross on different levels.

clue.text: Arbitrary and inconsiderate way to celebrate scoring a goal?

definitions.meaning: acting with overbearing disregard for others

definitions.text: way to celebrate scoring a goal?
definitions.meaning: read literally, slapping raised hands together, a high five after a goal

explanation.surface: Is a high-five after scoring an overbearing way to celebrate?
explanation.definitionFit: High-handed behaviour is overbearing and arbitrary; literally, hands raised high are a footballer's celebration.

clue.text: You start with a warning, if I were you, to be a sport

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
read literally, the letter I stands where the letter U (you) was

parts.note: achtung is German for attention, a warning cry

explanation.surface: Advice given with a cautionary 'if I were you' about taking up a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if I were you' is taken literally: in ACHTUNG the U (sounding like 'you') becomes I, giving ACHTING. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yachting, the racing or cruising of yachts, is a recognised sport.

clue.text: See 15
Loud protest over soldiers, each with gifts, new or otherwise, posing the unanswerable question

parts.note: a howl is a loud cry of protest
on in the sense of about or concerning, like over
GIs are American soldiers
apiece means each, as in a pound apiece

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so these letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A loud outcry about soldiers each receiving gifts, new or not, raises an impossible question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges the gift letters with N and OR to give the last word of the phrase, which ends the stock question.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock example of a question with no fixed answer, used when something has no set length.

clue.text: See 15
Painter, being poorly, put in months in Paris

indicators.note: the sickness word is put in among the French letters

parts.note: mai is French for May, so mais are Mays, months in French
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A painter who fell ill and spent several months recuperating in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link. Mai is the French for May, so its plural is loosely 'months in Paris'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Everett Millais was a Victorian painter, a founder of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.

clue.text: Tough about Circle Line appearing in films that back learning

indicators.note: the tough-and-circle group appears inside the films' word
back tells us the films word is read in reverse

parts.note: pics is informal for films, motion pictures

indicators.note: the tough word goes about, or around, the circle and line

parts.note: harsh means tough or severe
O is a circle by its shape

explanation.surface: A tough documentary about the London Underground's Circle Line in films that support education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the circle and line inside the tough word, giving HOLARSH; 'back' turns the films word into SCIP; 'appearing in' places one inside the other. 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship means academic learning, the knowledge of a scholar.

clue.text: Make new arrangements about class

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: Reorganising a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to reorganise, putting things on a new footing.

clue.text: See 9
Where to play cricket when not skating in the White House

parts.note: the Oval is a London cricket ground, home of Surrey
a skater who is not skating is off the ice

explanation.surface: Playing cricket rather than skating at the American president's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a famous Test cricket ground in south London. The definition is a place within the White House.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval Office is the US president's study inside the White House.

clue.text: Borough's best man should

definitions.meaning: a borough of east London; the 's stands for 'is'
a best man should have the wedding ring ready

explanation.surface: The district's best man ought to be prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: Havering is an outer London borough. Read as HAVE RING, it is what a best man must do at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Havering is a London borough; split in two, it is the best man's duty of having the ring.

clue.text: See 21
Time taken by a fast pressman with great ability

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A journalist with real flair takes time over his fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' is a link joining the pieces in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Talented means gifted, having great natural ability.

clue.text: Born scoundrel to talk of footwear

parts.note: a rogue is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A scoundrel born to chatter about shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. The definition plays on two senses: a brogue is an accent (a way of talking) and also a sturdy shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is both a regional accent, especially Irish, and a stout leather shoe, so footwear's name for a manner of speech.
